name: String Concatenation (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that prints the text "333", "63", and "36".

comments.content:
We could get the first string that we want to print by using the + operations to concatenate the string 3 with two integers (each with value 3). Since the first parameter is a string, everything rest will be a string concatenation.
The final string gets printed followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We could create the second string that we want to print by first adding the two integers (each with value 3) and then concatenating the result of numeric addition with the string 3. In this case, first left to right expression is evaluated (giving 3+3=6) and then string 3 is appended to result of that evaluation giving 63 as output.
The final string gets printed followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We could create the third string that we want to print by concatenating the string 3 with the result returned by adding two integers (each with value 3). We use parentheses to group the + operation with the two numeric operands. This forces that operation to happen first. Because both operands are numbers, the numbers are added in the arithmetic sense, producing the result 6. The integer 6 is then concatenated with the string 3, producing a larger string.
The final string gets printed followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
